item.title: Actor Model Frameworks for Distributed Systems: Orleans vs Akka.NET vs ProtoActor vs CAF
item.description:
What Is the Actor Model?

The Actor Model is a mathematical model for concurrent computation that treats “actors” as the universal primitives of computation. Each actor can make local decisions, create more actors, send messages, and determine how to respond to the next message received. The model naturally handles concurrency without locks, making it ideal for building distributed systems.

item.title: Self-Hosted Microservices Frameworks 2026: Dapr vs go-micro vs go-kit
item.description: Building microservices from scratch means reinventing service discovery, retries, pub/sub, and state management on every project. A good microservices framework abstracts these cross-cutting concerns so your team focuses on business logic. This guide compares three leading self-hosted frameworks: Dapr, go-micro, and go-kit — examining their architectures, deployment models, and real-world tradeoffs.
